app_record_conflict.description: Wire 3.2 Equal times, spec 4.2: two records of alice's wallet, signed with its signing key, with the same updated_at and different bodies (the endpoint identifiers in their Paykit member, protocols.paykit). Both verify; together they are a conflict for every reader, which uses neither and keeps the earlier record it holds, here the wallet app record of documents, until a record with a later updated_at. The switch refuses the second of them (the app_put steps of claims.json).

accepted.name: the member of a protocol no reader here knows: other

app_record_protocols.description: Wire 3.2 Protocols' members: the form of an app record's protocols, on documents.json's wallet app record with one member added beside Paykit's (or, last of refused, protocols itself replaced), signed again with the wallet's signing key. protocols is an object; each name has the syntax of a scope name, 1 to 32 characters of a-z, 0-9, _ and -, starting with a letter or digit; each value is an object, or null, which is no member. refused are records every reader refuses, the switch included; accepted are ones every reader takes, ignoring the member of a protocol it doesn't know, and Paykit's readers read the paykit member as before. protocols is the record's protocols member as signed. reason is the prototype's wording.

approval.description: Wire 3.10: the wallet's approval, the companion claim of its grant approval: the hash of its app request, its certificate, alice's identity.json version 3 listing it, and its full key bundle (data epochs 1 and 2 and the naming key), one part sealed with fixed randomness (seeds approval/cek, approval/nonce, approval/ikm-e) to its bundle key and signed by alice's identity key. It holds no key in the clear.

auth_request.description: Wire 3.9: the Pubky auth request the wallet's app request binds: its secret (only its hash is in the request), client ID, client key and capabilities.

description: Signed documents (wire 2.2, 3): carried as { "body": base64url of the exact JSON bytes, "sig": base64url }, in headers as "<body>.<sig>". Signed document bytes are lp(body bytes, signature); every hash over a document (certificate hashes in identity.json, chain item hashes, the freeze hash) is BLAKE3 of those bytes. Each identity.json names its signing install in signer, a 16-byte signer ID (seeds alice/signer and bob/signer).

discarded.description: Wire 3.6: the next service's signed answer that it discarded the import bound to the freeze, with the service key the freeze names (seed service/alice/next), and the unfreeze as the signer then sends it to the old service.

permission_rejections.description: Wire 3.1: certificates every verifier refuses, the switch included, for a permissions list that isn't well formed: a name that isn't a switch permission, a name twice, or names out of the fixed order. Each is the wallet certificate of documents with permissions changed, signed by alice's identity key; the signatures verify. reason is the prototype's wording at the switch.

scope_rule.description: Wire 3.1: the switch's scope rule, on documents.json's wallet certificate (scopes pay, contacts, manage_contacts) with scopes added and its permissions kept, signed by alice's identity key. A scope is name or name:<sub>: a name is 1 to 32 characters of a-z, 0-9, _ and -, starting with a letter or digit, and a sub has the syntax of a label; each once, never a name beside one of its name:<sub>, at most 32 in all. refused are certificates every verifier refuses, the switch included; accepted are ones the switch takes, and Paykit's verifiers too, ignoring the names they don't know. reason is the prototype's wording.
